svg.text: R3 — Scaling: two independent ladders, each with a measured trigger
Storage layout and retrieval algorithm are different axes — conflating them buys embeddings you never needed, on a layout that never changed.
climb a rung (one axis only)
instrument fires that trigger
STORAGE LADDER
how the index is FILED on disk
What does NOT change when the rung changes
• the resolver API — same call, same answer object
• the kb:index:check drift gate — it covers whichever
layout is live, byte-comparing a regenerated copy
• the caller: a skill, an agent, /qa-fix — none of them
can tell S1 from S2, and none of them has to
S2 · catalog + domain shards
knowledge-index.json becomes a catalog: counts,
shard map, domain vocabulary, schemaVersion 2
records move into index/<domain>.json shards
resolver reads the catalog + ONLY the shards whose
domain vocabulary intersects the query tokens
TRIGGER — MEASURED, NOT DECIDED
the index file would exceed 256 KB or 1,000 entries
(defaults in brain.json, tunable). gen-index.mjs picks
the layout from the measured size — migration is automatic
S1 · one file (where every brain starts)
one knowledge-index.json per knowledge root
generated, never hand-edited; carries the typed
frontmatter, file path + line range, citedBy count
the resolver loads that single file and scores over it
S2a below is NOT a third rung — it ships from day one,
alongside whichever of S1 / S2 happens to be live.
THE INSTRUMENTS
one per ladder — and they never talk
exam.mjs
human-owned goldens — questions a person
wrote, with the entry that should win
reports hit@1 / hit@3 / hit@k and MRR,
and splits a miss into TWO diseases:
wrongPlace
— found, ranked too low
notFound
— never appeared at all
a ranking problem and a coverage problem
are not the same problem
FIRES THE RETRIEVAL LADDER
gen-index.mjs
measures two numbers at generation time:
the index size in bytes, and entry count
no judgement, no opinion about retrieval
quality — it only sees how big the file got
FIRES THE STORAGE LADDER
Different instruments. Different questions.
Storage never asks “are we finding things?”
Retrieval never asks “is the file big?”
So the rungs move on their own schedules, and
in a real brain they usually do: sharding is
reached by growth, A2 by measured misses.
A big corpus that answers well stays on A1.
A small corpus that answers badly earns A2.
RETRIEVAL LADDER
how a topic query is ANSWERED
A3 · hybrid vector (opt-in, never yet reached)
a local embeddings sidecar index/embeddings.f32 +
an embedder passport, merged with the lexical
score by RRF (reciprocal rank fusion)
the journal shape — brute-force cosine over a
sidecar file — NOT a vector database
breaks zero-dep AND determinism
TRIGGER — THREE CONDITIONS, ALL REQUIRED
after synonyms the exam STILL shows a notFound ceiling
that lexical ranking cannot lift · the corpus is several
thousand entries · the operator explicitly opts in
A2 · BM25 + curated synonyms
zero-dep BM25 in pure JS over the same fields —
term saturation and length normalisation done right
plus synonyms.json per brain, owned by the team:
PLP ⇒ product listing page, корзина ⇒ cart
still zero-dep · still deterministic · still exam-gateable
TRIGGER
exam misses classified notFound trace to a VOCABULARY
MISMATCH — the question’s words are genuinely absent
from the entry that nonetheless holds the answer
A1 · weighted lexical overlap (today)
title 6 / tags 4 / kind 2 / body 1, length-damped;
subject and aliases are first-class scored fields
zero-dep · deterministic · ties broken by id
S2a · catalog.md — parallel to the ladder, not a rung on it
A generated one-line-per-entry digest: id · kind · status · title · tags. It ships from day one next to the index, is
regenerated by kb:index and byte-checked by the same --check gate, and is unaffected by whether S1 or S2 is live.
The v1 gap it closes:
kb-guard exempts Bash-less subagents from escalation — they cannot run the resolver, so
denying them would only wedge them. But v1 gave them no door either: exempt, and empty-handed.
Progressive disclosure:
read the small catalog, then Read the ONE entry file it names — the same three-tier
pattern as Agent Skills and Claude Code’s own MEMORY.md index. Never the whole corpus into context.
The rule: a rung is climbed on exam evidence, never on appetite
BM25 wins outright on exact identifiers, error codes and rare terms; RRF’s margin over plain BM25 is real but modest
(NDCG 0.7068 vs 0.6983 on a standard corpus). Our dominant query shape is an id — and ids ARE the citation contract
the suite CSVs point at. So lexical stays the exact-id layer forever; embeddings could only ever be added beside it.
Cortex’s own numbers agree: model-free rules moved hits 53.3% → 60% and MRR 0.308 → 0.403, while its
trained reranker gave +0.007 MRR and was switched off as overfitting.
One client brain, two coordinates
its position on each axis moves separately
S1
S2
A3
A2
A1
not taken — no measured ceiling
1 ~40 entries — one index file, lexical overlap
2 ~1,200 — gen-index.mjs shards automatically;
retrieval is untouched and nobody is asked
3 ~2,600 — the exam’s notFound cluster earns A2;
storage does not move at all
